description: Wire the shared battle-enhancements logic into the backend /battle handler. The handler now accepts {monsterId, difficulty, seed}, regenerates the IDENTICAL enemy via the shared generateEnemy(playerStage, difficulty, seed) (so the client preview and the actual fight match exactly), simulates, applies the difficulty-scaled reward on a win, updates the persisted win/loss record via the shared recordBattleOutcome, keeps the #42 battle-win affection bump, defaults the record on load for legacy saves, and returns {result, monster}. Depends on FEAT-002.
steps: Edit packages/backend/src/handlers/battle.ts. Replace the local buildEnemy(player) with a call to the shared generateEnemy(player.stageId, difficulty, seed) imported from @ddm/shared. Remove the now-unused buildEnemy (or keep nothing dead).

Parse the POST body to read difficulty and seed in addition to monsterId: `const body = parseBody<{ monsterId?: string; difficulty?: Difficulty; seed?: number }>(...)`. Validate monsterId as today (400 if missing). Default difficulty to "normal" when absent/invalid (guard against unknown strings; only accept "easy"|"normal"|"hard"). Default seed to a server-generated value (e.g. Date.now()) ONLY if the client did not send one — but note that for preview==fight to hold, the client WILL send the seed; document that an absent seed means no client preview was shown.

After loading + reviveMonster(player) as today, build the enemy with the shared function using the SAME seed that will be passed to simulateBattle. Pass that same seed into simulateBattle(player, enemy, seed) so the deterministic enemy and the deterministic sim are both reproducible from the request.

On the result: start from the revived player with hp = result.playerHpAfter and lastUpdatedAt = now, as today. On result.winner === "player", apply the difficulty-scaled reward from shared battleReward(difficulty, true) to atk/def (replacing the current hardcoded +1/+1), THEN keep the existing recordBattleWinAffection(updated, now) #42 bump. For every outcome (win/lose/draw) call shared recordBattleOutcome(updated, result.winner, now) to update the persisted win/loss/draw/streak record.
Keep clampStats + reviveMonster(updated, now) exactly as today so a loss never strands the monster at 0 HP.

On load, ensure the persisted monster's battleRecord is defaulted for legacy saves before use: apply shared normalizeBattleRecord to the loaded player (or rely on recordBattleOutcome's internal battleRecordOf defaulting) so an old save without the field persists back WITH a zeroed-then-updated record. Choose and document one path; the simplest is: recordBattleOutcome already defaults via battleRecordOf, so the returned monster always has a full record.
Keep the response shape ok({ result, monster: updated }). Do not change http.ts/dynamo.ts.
Run `npm run build` to typecheck the backend against the new shared exports (the backend bundles @ddm/shared, so a mismatch fails here).
Run `npm test` to confirm shared tests still pass (no backend unit test harness exists; the backend is validated via typecheck/build and the shared tests covering the pure logic it calls).
acceptance_criteria: battle.ts no longer defines buildEnemy; it calls shared generateEnemy(player.stageId, difficulty, seed).

The handler accepts {monsterId, difficulty, seed}, defaults difficulty to normal and validates it, and uses the same seed for both generateEnemy and simulateBattle so the enemy is reproducible from the request.
A win applies battleReward(difficulty,true) deltas (difficulty-scaled, replacing the fixed +1/+1) and still applies the #42 recordBattleWinAffection bump.
Every outcome updates the persisted record via recordBattleOutcome; the returned/persisted monster always has a full battleRecord even for a legacy save that lacked one.
`npm run build` succeeds and `npm test` is green.
findings:
Wired packages/backend/src/handlers/battle.ts to the FEAT-002 shared logic. Changes: (1) POST body parsed as { monsterId?, difficulty?, seed? }; kept the 400 when monsterId missing/empty. (2) difficulty resolved via resolveDifficulty() which only accepts easy|normal|hard and otherwise defaults to normal (guards unknown strings). (3) seed = client seed when a number, else Date.now(); the SAME seed is passed to both generateEnemy and simulateBattle so enemy+sim are reproducible from the request (preview==fight). (4) Removed the local buildEnemy; enemy now = generateEnemy(player.stageId, difficulty, seed). (5) On winner===player, applied battleReward(difficulty,true) deltas to atk/def (replacing hardcoded +1/+1) THEN kept recordBattleWinAffection(updated, now) (#42 bump). (6) recordBattleOutcome(updated, result.winner, now) called for EVERY outcome to persist wins/losses/draws/streak. (7) Kept clampStats + reviveMonster(updated, now) exactly as before so a loss never strands at 0 HP; response shape unchanged ok({ result, monster: updated }). http.ts/dynamo.ts untouched.

Legacy-save defaulting path chosen: rely on recordBattleOutcome's internal battleRecordOf defaulting (did NOT add normalizeBattleRecord on load, to keep the diff minimal). Verified recordBattleOutcome returns a monster with a full battleRecord, and the downstream clampStats + reviveMonster (cloneMonster uses spread) preserve battleRecord, so the persisted/returned monster always carries a full record even for a pre-#41 save that lacked the field. BattleResult.winner is "player"|"enemy"|"draw" which maps directly onto recordBattleOutcome's BattleWinner param (no translation needed). No shared-logic bugs found; FEAT-002 left untouched.

Verification: `npm run build` succeeds (shared -> backend bundle -> frontend tsc+vite -> infra all typecheck). `npm test` green at 94 passing (unchanged from FEAT-002 baseline). No backend unit-test harness exists; backend validated via typecheck/build + shared tests covering the pure logic it calls. No new runtime dependencies.
